issue.title: Generalize Eq. (16) to rational profiles and find the parameters for 1e-6

milestone.title: G8 · Other paths
milestone.description: Alternatives to our formulation and methods (the RT variables of arXiv:2611.07007, Fourier speed, low D from first principles), the large-D expansion to higher orders, and the complex scalar.

issue.body:
**What.** Generalize arXiv:2611.07007v1 Eq. (16), β̃ = A* Re[z/(1 + wz²)] with z = e^{iθ}, to the rational family β̃ = A* Re[z P_L(z²)/Q_N(z²)]. Fit it to the D = ∞ tuned profile's harmonics (`solver/eeg_profile/data/tuned_profile_A2.72.txt`), and find the smallest (L, N) that reaches 1e-6 relative at every ν ≤ 19. The gist (https://gist.github.com/nmoinvaz/6dadeb33f79fe099252134862ce8dce8, steps 8) and notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §3.3 show [1/1] within 2.9%.

**Why.** The true ratios r_ν approach their limit like ν⁻³, the sign of a simple nearest pole pair. So [L/1] should converge as L grows, and the parameter count it needs measures how far the echo is from a one-pole profile.

**Acceptance (can fail).** A planted profile with known (L, N) is recovered through the same fit code, with the criterion written first. A table of the maximum relative error against (L, N). The pole positions of the best fit, against the profile's nearest singularity at 1.5344 ∓ 1.4284i (paper's gauge).

**Depends on.** Nothing.

comments.body: started, a subagent of the coordinator on mac (Apple M5), in its own git worktree, 2 processes at nice 10. WIP branch wip/i133, raw folder I133-mac/. It posts its own progress and closing summary here; the coordinator closes the issue after review.

Progress (mac, subagent, 2 processes at nice 10). cpu: 2 of 10 threads; memory under 200 MB per process.

Scripts on wip/i133 (6b7377c): `solver/eeg_profile/rational_fit.py` (Padé, relative least squares and Lawson minimax fits of [L/N], L + N ≤ 8, to c_k = C_{2k+1}/C_1 for ν ≤ 19 at 60 digits; poles in θ, paper's gauge) and `rational_controls.py`. The planted criteria were committed (e973bb9) before the first run.

Planted [2/3]: recovered as the unique smallest family, max error 2e-15, poles and zeros to 1e-13 (exit 0). Controls: the wrong gauge fails the pole check only, dropping ν = 11 fails every check (exit 1 each).

Real data, first numbers (A = 2.72, K = 45): Padé reaches 1e-6 for no L + N ≤ 8 ([4/4] 1.15e-6 at ν = 19, where the A series' remainder estimate of the data is 5.4e-7). Least squares and minimax reach it first at L + N = 7, for [4/3], [3/4] and [2/5] (8 complex parameters for 10 harmonics). Every fit with L + N ≥ 5 puts its nearest pole at 1.5341–1.5344 − 1.42839…1.42848i, on the profile's 1.5344 − 1.4284i.

One planted check fails as stated. The pole-march test's meromorphic plant moves its second pole by 0.025 between [3/3] and [4/4], against the 0.02 required for "converged", though it lands within 0.002 of the planted pole and does not march. The threshold is kept, and the failure goes into the note.

Next: sensitivity runs (A = 2.71918, the tail estimate added), then the note section.

**Closing summary** (mac, subagent, 2 processes at nice 10, 07:23–07:48 UTC; cpu at most 2 of 10 threads, under 200 MB per process). The issue stays open for the coordinator's review.

**Answer.** The family A* Re[z P_L(z²)/Q_N(z²)] reaches 1e-6 at every ν ≤ 19 first at **L + N = 7**, for [3/4], [4/3] and [2/5] fitted by least squares or minimax. That is 8 complex parameters for 10 complex harmonics. Padé (exact matching) reaches it for no L + N ≤ 8 on the stored data: [4/4] is off by 1.15e-6 at ν = 19, where the data's own A-series remainder estimate is 5.4e-7. Each added complex parameter lowers the error by a factor of about 7.

**What ran** (scripts on wip/i133, from `solver/eeg_profile`; logs in raw folder `I133-mac/`):

| command | exit |
|---|---|
| `rational_fit.py` (A = 2.72, both J, Padé + least squares + minimax) | 0 (checks S, D pass) |
| `rational_fit.py --tail` (the A series' tail estimate added) | 0 |
| `rational_fit.py --A 2.71918` | 0 |
| `rational_fit.py --plant=rational` | 0 |
| `rational_fit.py --plant=rational --mutate=gauge` and `--mutate=drop` | 1 each, as they must |
| `rational_fit.py --plant=branch` | 0 |
| `rational_fit.py --plant=poles` | 1, a reported failure (below) |
| `rational_controls.py` | 0, "all controls behave" |

**Max relative error at ν ≤ 19, the best family per total degree** (`rational_fit.py`, real_A2.72.log; complex error |m/c − 1|):

| L + N | complex params | Padé | least squares | minimax |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (Eq. 16) | 2 | [0/1] 3.28e-1 | [0/1] 3.50e-2 | [0/1] 2.16e-2 |
| 2 | 3 | [1/1] 4.69e-2 | [1/1] 5.19e-3 | [1/1] 3.37e-3 |
| 3 | 4 | [1/2] 7.75e-3 | [1/2] 7.82e-4 | [1/2] 5.17e-4 |
| 4 | 5 | [2/2] 1.66e-3 | [2/2] 1.19e-4 | [2/2] 9.26e-5 |
| 5 | 6 | [2/3] 3.12e-4 | [2/3] 1.60e-5 | [2/3] 1.22e-5 |
| 6 | 7 | [3/3] 5.27e-5 | [3/3] 2.39e-6 | [3/3] 1.78e-6 |
| 7 | 8 | [3/4] 5.82e-6 | [3/4] 2.80e-7 | [3/4] 2.17e-7 |
| 8 | 9 | [4/4] 1.15e-6 | [4/4] 6.18e-8 | [3/5] 4.97e-8 |

With `--tail` the least-squares and minimax verdict is the same (L + N = 7, the same three families), and Padé reaches 1e-6 at L + N = 8 ([4/4] 3.13e-7). At A = 2.71918 nothing changes. The full (L, N) matrix is in notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §8.4.

**Poles against the profile's singularity.** All 78 fits with L + N ≥ 5 put the nearest pole at 1.53412–1.53439 − (1.42839–1.42848)i. The 18 that reach 1e-6 put it at 1.53437–1.53439 − 1.42839i, on the profile's 1.5344 ∓ 1.4284i (paper's gauge). In the repository's gauge that is 3.1049–3.1052 ∓ 1.4284i.

The further poles are not a second singularity. They pair with zeros 0.001–0.08 away, carry residues of 0.5–8% of the nearest pole's, and line up at Re θ ≈ 1.55–1.61. They also march toward the singularity as the order grows: the second pole of the Padé [n/n] goes 1.607 − 2.113i, 1.560 − 1.775i, 1.543 − 1.646i for n = 2, 3, 4, like the planted pole-plus-logarithm profile. With the tail added, (k + 1.5)⁴|r_{k+1} − r_k| = 0.01124 for ν = 11–17 to four digits, a power law, which a single further pole cannot give. So the fits need more structure than poles: a branch point at the nearest singularity, plausibly a (θ − θ₀) ln(θ − θ₀) term beside the simple pole (numerical evidence).

**Controls.**
- Planted [2/3], with the criterion committed (e973bb9) before the run: recovered as the unique smallest family, error 2.3e-15 (Padé) and 5.6e-17 (least squares), poles to 3.3e-14. The wrong gauge fails the pole check only. Dropping ν = 11 fails every check.
- Check S (nearest pole within 1e-3 of the reference) passes 78 of 78, and the gauge mutation fails it.
- Check D (the data file reproduced) passes, and the A mutation fails it.
- The pole-march test: the branch plant marches (pass).

**Discrepancies, reported, not fixed.**
1. The pole-march test's meromorphic plant fails the "converged" half as stated. It moved 0.025 from [3/3] to [4/4], against 0.02 required, though it lands 0.002 from the planted pole and does not march. The threshold was not loosened, so the test certifies marching but not convergence.
2. Check D first passed vacuously. The data file's leading blank line paired the inputs one block off, so the first input was compared with nothing. Its mutation exposed this, and ed08568 fixed it. The fits did not depend on it.
3. The issue reads the ν⁻³ law as "a simple nearest pole pair". The leading term is a simple pole, but a power-law approach itself means a weaker singularity at the same point. A pole with only farther singularities gives an exponential approach.
4. §3.3's [1/1] "2.9% at ν = 19" is a modulus error. The complex error, phase included, is 4.7%.

**Commits.** wip/i133 at 24da6fa: rational_fit.py, rational_controls.py and notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §8, which has the proposed text in §8.8. Raw folder I133-mac at 9c12362 of choptuik-large-d-raw (merged as 6e48212). mutation_controls.py does not yet call rational_controls.py (task 5 below).

**Recommended tasks**

1. **The singularity type of the D = ∞ profile, from the inner equations.** *What:* a local expansion of the D = ∞ inner equations about θ₀ = 1.5344 − 1.4284i (paper's gauge). Find whether the profile there is a simple pole plus (θ − θ₀) ln(θ − θ₀), a logarithm at a resonance, or an algebraic (θ − θ₀)^α. *Why:* §8.5's fits and power law point to a pole with a weaker branch at the same point. Ten harmonics cannot settle its type, and #137 and #138 depend on it. *Acceptance (can fail):* the expansion predicts the exponent of |r_{ν+2} − r_ν| ∝ (ν + 2)⁻⁴ and its constant, 0.01124 in (k + 1.5)⁴|r_{k+1} − r_k|, within a tolerance stated first. A planted ODE with a known logarithmic singularity is recovered, and with the logarithm removed the check fails. *Depends on:* #133.
2. **A pole-plus-logarithm family through rational_fit's code path.** *What:* G(u) = P_L(u)/(1 − u/u₀) + (1 − u/u₀) ln(1 − u/u₀) B_M(u) with u₀ free, fitted by the same least-squares and minimax code to ν ≤ 19, giving a table of the maximum error against (L, M) next to §8.4's. *Why:* if the singularity carries a logarithm, this is the compact family and the natural trial form for #138. *Acceptance (can fail):* a planted pole-plus-logarithm profile is recovered to 1e-12 with its (L, M) as the unique smallest family. The control B = 0 misses 1e-6 at the same parameter count. On the real data, report whether some family with fewer than 8 complex parameters reaches 1e-6. *Depends on:* #133.
3. **A pole-march test that can certify convergence.** *What:* restate §8.3's test so that its "converged" half passes a meromorphic plant. Use more orders, or the step ratio over [L/2] rows, with the criterion written before it runs on both plants and then on the real data. *Why:* "the further poles march" now rests on the marching half alone. A working convergence half would rule out a nearby genuine second pole. *Acceptance (can fail):* the meromorphic plant passes "converged", the branch plant fails it, and the real data's class is reported with the criterion unchanged. A finding that 10 harmonics are too few for any such criterion is a valid outcome. *Depends on:* #133. Task 4 helps.
4. **Resolve the tuned harmonics to ν = 25 or beyond.** *What:* extend the A series past K = 45, or bound its remainder with a planted check of the geometric tail estimate behind `--tail`. Then rerun rational_fit.py with ν ≤ 23 fitted. *Why:* at ν = 19 the 1e-6 target is within a factor 2 of the data's remainder estimate, and Padé's verdict changes with the tail. *Acceptance (can fail):* the ν = 19 remainder estimate falls below 1e-7, and the K = 47 sums agree with the K = 45 tail-corrected sums within the estimate. A mutated tail (ratio doubled) fails that agreement. *Depends on:* the K = 45 scan setup (solver/inner_amp). That run took about 14 h on 3 processes.
5. **Call rational_controls.py from mutation_controls.py.** *What:* add the rational rows to `solver/eeg_profile/mutation_controls.py`, the coordinator's file. *Acceptance (can fail):* it prints "all controls behave" with the rows included, and exits 1 when one rational mutation is made to pass. *Depends on:* #133 merged.

Coordinator review. I reran `rational_controls.py`: exit 0, all controls behave. Merged into main as 79fb5de (solver/eeg_profile/rational_fit.py, rational_controls.py; notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §8). Verdict: rational [L/N] families reach 1e-6 at every ν ≤ 19 at L + N = 7 ([3/4], [4/3], [2/5]), each added complex parameter cutting the error about 7×. Every resolving fit puts the nearest pole on the profile's 1.5344 ∓ 1.4284i. The further poles track a branch point there, not a second singularity (numerical evidence). The discrepancies are noted, including §3.3's 2.9% being modulus-only (4.7% with the phase). The recommended tasks are #150–#154, and the guidance for #137 and #138 is posted there.
